title: Dolma biber
subtitle: Turkish stuffed peppers with rice, lamb, and herbs
excerpt: Turkish stuffed peppers are filled with spiced lamb mince and rice, closed with their caps, and braised in a light tomato and olive oil sauce. The rice absorbs the juices from the lamb and the pepper as it cooks, becoming richly savoury and fragrant. They are a classic of Turkish home cooking.
sourceNotes: Dolma (stuffed vegetables) are a central part of Turkish and wider Middle Eastern cooking. The pepper version is one of the most common, appearing at home tables across Turkey.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze after cooking. Reheat gently in a covered pan with a splash of water.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Cook up to 2 days ahead and reheat. The flavours improve after a day in the fridge.

content.text: Dolma means stuffed in Turkish and covers a whole category of dishes from courgettes to cabbage leaves to peppers. The pepper version is perhaps the most accessible and produces a satisfying, self-contained meal that only needs a bowl of yoghurt alongside.

The filling is raw rice mixed with cooked lamb mince and herbs; the rice finishes cooking as the peppers braise in their sauce. This means the rice absorbs the lamb juices and the sweet pepper liquid rather than just water, which gives the filling a richness that pre-cooked rice cannot match.
Slice the tops off neatly and keep them as lids. Pack the filling loosely; the rice will expand as it cooks and over-filled peppers can split.

items.prepNote: tops sliced off and reserved, seeds removed

content.text: Warm the olive oil in a frying pan over medium heat. Add the onion and cook for 6 minutes until soft. Add the garlic and lamb mince and break up the meat. Cook for 5 minutes until the lamb has lost its pink colour. Stir in the tomato puree, spices, mint, salt, and parsley. Cook for 2 more minutes, then remove from the heat. Stir in the raw rinsed rice. Mix well.

Mix the tinned tomatoes, stock, olive oil, and salt together for the braising sauce. Pour a little into the base of the casserole dish. Spoon the filling loosely into each pepper to about three-quarters full to allow for the rice to expand. Set the lid back on each pepper. Stand them upright in the casserole and pour the remaining sauce around them. Bring to a gentle simmer over the hob, cover, and cook over a low heat for 45 minutes until the rice is fully cooked and the peppers are very tender.

rows.symptom: Rice still crunchy after cooking time
rows.cause: Filling packed too tightly or too little liquid
rows.fix: Add another 100 ml of hot stock or water, cover, and continue cooking for 10 to 15 minutes.

rows.cause: Overfilled or cooked at too high a heat
rows.fix: Fill to three-quarters only and keep the heat very low. The rice expands significantly.

rows.cause: Too little sauce or sauce evaporated
rows.fix: There should always be some sauce bubbling around the peppers. Check and add a splash of water if needed.

content.text: Use yellow or red peppers for a sweeter result. Courgettes can be hollowed and stuffed in exactly the same way. For a vegetarian version, replace the lamb with finely chopped mushrooms and walnuts.
Dolma biber reheats very well. The flavours deepen overnight in the fridge. Cook up to 2 days ahead, refrigerate, and reheat gently in the covered pan with a splash of water.

Stuffed vegetables are woven through Turkish home cooking and appear at mezze, as a main course, and cold as part of a spread. Dolma biber is made in every household, and every family has a slightly different spice mix. In summer, courgettes and aubergines get the same treatment; in winter, dried peppers are used.
